title_ar: الشيخ الددو يشرف على افتتاح قسم الاقتصاد الإسلامي بجامعة ابن ياسين
title_en: Sheikh al-Dedew Presides over the Opening of the Islamic Economics Department at Ibn Yasin University
body_ar:
احتضن مقر جامعة عبد الله بن ياسين بنواكشوط مساء اليوم الثلاثاء 25 محرم 1433 الموافق: 20/12/2011 حفلا رسميا لإطلاق قسم الاقتصاد الإسلامي بالجامعة.

وقد أشرف رئيس الجامعة فضيلة الشيخ محمد الحسن ولد الددو على افتتاح القسم بحضور الطاقم الإداري والعلمي بالجامعة وجمهور من طلبتها ومهتمين بالشأن العلمي، وقد افتتح الحفل من طرف منسق قسم الاقتصاد الإسلامي المستحدث الدكتور محمد ولد سيد أوبك مرحبا بالرئيس وطاقم الجامعة وبالجمهور الحاضر، مذكرا بأهمية إطلاق الجامعة هذا القسم الذي يفتتح لأول مرة في البلاد، ويبدأ باستقبال الطلبة حملة كل من الباكلوريا والليصانص، حيث يقدم لهم تكوينا أكاديميا حرصت الجامعة على أن يكون خاضعا للمقاييس العلمية المعتمدة في هذا المجال.

ثم أحيلت الكلمة إلى رئيس الجامعة فضيلة الشيخ محمد الحسن ولد الددو الذي نوه بافتتاح الجامعة لقسمها الجديد الذي يكمل مختلف التكوينات التي تجري فيها الدراسة داخل الجامعة، وهنأ الطاقم الإداري على تذليله كل الصعاب في سبيل فتح قسم يعنى بالبحث في مجال حيوي كالاقتصاد الإسلامي، وقدم الشيخ خلال كلمته الرسمية باسم الجامعة شكره للحكومة والسلطات العمومية على تعاونها مع الجامعة، آملا أن يتعزز هذا التعاون حتى تحقق الجامعة طموحاتها في تعليم أكاديمي عصري متكامل، متطلعا لأن تقدم الجامعة من خلال قسم الاقتصاد الإسلامي الاستشارات العلمية التي تحتاجها البنوك الإسلامية العاملة في البلد، مما يساهم في حل بعض الإشكالات المطروحة للعاملين في مجال الصيرفة الإسلامية في مختلف دول العالم.

بدوره تناول الحديث نائب رئيس الجامعة الدكتور محمد سالم ولد الخو مرحبا بالحضور وشاكرا فضيلة الشيخ على الاهتمام الذي يوليه للتحصيل العلمي من خلال افتتاحه لهذا القسم اليوم، كما شكر الدكاترة على التعاون الذي ما فتئوا يقدموه من أجل تحقيق رسالة جامعة ابن ياسين، والجهود العلمية والبحثية التي يقومون بها لتطوير أداء الجامعة والرفع من مستوى خريجيها في مختلف الأقسام والتخصصات.

وفي الأخير فتح الباب للجمهور؛ حيث تداعى إلى المنصة عدد من الدكاترة المدرسين بالجامعة، معبرين عن شكرهم للجامعة على افتتاح هذا القسم، بدورهم أكد المتدخلون من الطلبة على أهمية هذا القسم؛ مسجلين أن الجامعة حازت قصب السبق بافتتاحها هذا القسم المعني بالاقتصاد الإسلامي.

لمتابعة الكلمة الافتتاحية اضغط هنا:
body_en:
The premises of ʿAbd Allah ibn Yasin University in Nouakchott hosted, on the evening of today, Tuesday 25 Muharram 1433, corresponding to 20/12/2011, an official ceremony for the launch of the university's Islamic economics department.

The university's president, His Eminence Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan Ould al-Dedew, presided over the opening of the department, in the presence of the university's administrative and academic staff and an audience of its students and of those interested in scholarly affairs. The ceremony was opened by the coordinator of the newly created Islamic economics department, Dr Muhammad Ould Sid Oubek, who welcomed the president, the university's staff and the audience present, recalling the importance of the university's launching this department, which is being opened for the first time in the country and which begins by receiving students holding the baccalaureate and the licence, offering them an academic training which the university has been careful to make conform to the scholarly standards adopted in this field.

The floor then passed to the university's president, His Eminence Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan Ould al-Dedew, who drew attention to the university's opening of its new department, which completes the various courses of training studied within the university, and congratulated the administrative staff on smoothing away every difficulty in the way of opening a department concerned with research in a field as vital as Islamic economics. In his formal address on behalf of the university the Sheikh offered his thanks to the government and the public authorities for their cooperation with the university, expressing the hope that this cooperation would be strengthened so that the university might realise its ambitions for a complete modern academic education, and looking forward to the university's providing, through the Islamic economics department, the scholarly consultancy needed by the Islamic banks operating in the country — thereby contributing to the resolution of some of the problems raised for those working in the field of Islamic banking in the various countries of the world.

In turn the university's vice-president, Dr Muhammad Salim Ould al-Khu, took the floor, welcoming those present and thanking His Eminence the Sheikh for the attention he gives to scholarly attainment through his opening of this department today. He also thanked the doctors for the cooperation they have never ceased to give towards realising the mission of Ibn Yasin University, and for the scholarly and research efforts they make to develop the university's performance and to raise the level of its graduates in its various departments and specialisms.

Finally the floor was opened to the audience, and a number of the doctors teaching at the university came forward to the platform, expressing their thanks to the university for opening this department. In their turn the students who spoke affirmed the importance of this department, recording that the university had taken the lead in opening this department concerned with Islamic economics.

flags.arabic: متطلعا لأن تقدم الجامعة من خلال قسم الاقتصاد الإسلامي الاستشارات العلمية التي تحتاجها البنوك الإسلامية العاملة في البلد
flags.context: the Sheikh's hope for the new department
options: render as a hope for the department, as the Arabic has it
render as an undertaking that the department will advise the banks
flags.note: متطلعا is 'looking forward to', a hope expressed in a speech, not a commitment and certainly not an endorsement of any bank or product. In English, a sentence in which a named jurist looks forward to his university advising Islamic banks is one step from being read as his approving those banks, which the record nowhere says and which would matter. The hope is kept as a hope. No ruling of any kind on banking practice appears in this record.

flags.arabic: الدكتور محمد ولد سيد أوبك / الدكتور محمد سالم ولد الخو
flags.context: the department coordinator and the vice-president
options: Muhammad Ould Sid Oubek / Muhammad Salim Ould al-Khu
Mohamed Ould Sidi Oubeck / Mohamed Salem Ould El Khou
flags.note: Neither man's own Latin-script spelling is known from the record, and Mauritanian names are conventionally written in a French-based orthography that does not follow from the Arabic. The forms used are provisional. A reviewer with access to the university's own materials should settle them.

flags.context: the qualifications the department's entrants hold
flags.note: Both words are borrowings from French into Mauritanian Arabic and name French-system qualifications: the baccalauréat completes secondary schooling and the licence is the first university degree. Option 3 explains them but by mapping them onto Anglophone equivalents that are not exact. The French forms are kept, since the record is describing a French-system institution.

flags.context: the field the department is to serve
flags.note: صيرفة is banking as a practice or trade, distinguished in the same paragraph from البنوك الإسلامية, the banks themselves. Both are kept distinct in the English. Not in the glossary, and it will recur wherever the corpus touches on finance.

translator_notes: A news report of an official ceremony. No ruling is stated anywhere in it and the five-rulings mapping of style guide section 3 is not engaged. This is worth stating plainly because the record's subject is Islamic economics and a reader may come to it expecting rulings on finance: there are none here.
The CMS timestamp is a bulk-upload date and is not evidence of when the report was written. Here the body's hijri and Gregorian dates agree with each other and with the timestamp.
Nothing in the record is quoted. Everything attributed to the Sheikh, to the coordinator and to the vice-president is the news desk's summary of what each said.
جامعة عبد الله بن ياسين is named in full at first mention and as Ibn Yasin University thereafter, following the source, which does the same.

The closing 'to follow the opening address click here' is the site's navigation furniture; preserved in body_ar, recorded in source_download_link, omitted from body_en. The opening address itself is audio and is not in this record.
